title: Multi-Agent Orchestrator workflow
description: GENERATED — do not edit. Run `python3 build_schema.py` after changing app/keys.json or app/vocabulary.json. This exists so your editor can tell you which keys are legal, which are required and what values they take, before you deploy rather than after.

$schema.description: Points your editor at this file.

$comment.description: Orientation for whoever opens the file. Not read by anything.

agents.description:
One entry per agent, keyed by agent id.

One entry per agent, keyed by agent id, which must match ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$ (no hyphens — the id becomes part of an AgentCore Runtime name). For `main` and `dedicated` the id is also the folder name under app/subagents/. FOUR KEYS ARE ON EVERY AGENT regardless of placement — name, kind, runtime, produces — and everything after them depends on `runtime`: a local agent has the model group, a remote one has the remote group, and neither has the other's. That is deliberate rather than untidy. A remote agent's `maxTokens` would read as governing its cost while doing nothing, because the model call happens on the far side of a trust boundary.

name.description:
Display name, shown on the diagram, in the timeline and on a review gate.

Read by: registry.py -> agent.name; bff/workflow.py; the UI node title

kind.description:
Whether the step completes inline or is long-running. Presentation only today: the UI shows a chip when it is not "sync".

Read by: registry.py -> agent.kind; bff/workflow.py ships it; index.html renders the chip

Default: "sync"

runtime.description:
Where the step runs. "main" = in-process; "dedicated" = its own AgentCore Runtime; "a2a" = an agent you do NOT operate, reached over the Agent2Agent protocol. Defaults to "main".

Read by: registry.py, subagent_runtimes.tf / orchestrator-stack.ts; the UI chip

Allowed values (runtimes in app/vocabulary.json): 'main', 'dedicated', 'a2a'

Default: "main"

produces.description:
The name of this agent's deliverable, e.g. "claim-decision". Names the asset type, is injected into the task prompt, and is what the framework stamps as `assetType` on the asset.

Read by: nodes.py task prompt; a2a_agent.py _as_asset (the envelope on a remote reply)

model.description:
Bedrock model id for THIS agent. Omit to use orchestrator.defaultModel — no shipped agent sets it; the mechanism is here for when one step needs a bigger model.

Read by: registry.py -> agent.model -> ctx.llm

temperature.description:
Sampling temperature. Defaults to 0, which is what you want for an agent that emits a structured asset.

Read by: registry.py -> agent.temperature

Default: 0

maxTokens.description:
Output token budget. Required, because too low does not surface as "budget exceeded" — it surfaces as an unparseable asset, so the number belongs in front of you rather than defaulted in code.

Read by: registry.py -> agent.max_tokens

Default: 4000

source.description:
Reach the A2A server this framework deploys for you, instead of an external URL. The deploy injects its endpoint, so there is nothing to commit. Exclusive with agentCard.

Read by: registry.py A2A_SOURCES; a2a.tf / orchestrator-stack.ts inject A2A_ENDPOINTS

Allowed values (a2aSources in app/vocabulary.json): 'a2a_lambda'

agentCard.description:
An external agent's base URL or Agent Card URL. Must be https:// — the request may carry a bearer token. Exclusive with source.

Read by: a2a_agent.py; validated in all three planes

skill.description:
Which of the shipped stand-in's skills this agent is. Only meaningful with `source`: an external agent advertises its own skills in its Agent Card.

Read by: a2a.tf / orchestrator-stack.ts, as the path segment of the injected endpoint

Allowed values (a2aLambdaSkills in app/vocabulary.json): 'compliance', 'resilience', 'analysis', 'recommendation'

Default: "compliance"

auth.description:
How this deployment authenticates TO the remote agent. Must be "sigv4" with `source`, because that endpoint is IAM-authed. A bearer token never goes here — it is injected by the IaC, keyed by agent id.

Read by: a2a_agent.py; validated in all three planes

Allowed values (a2aAuthModes in app/vocabulary.json): 'none', 'bearer', 'oauth2', 'sigv4'

Default: "none"

tool.description:
A key in the `tools` block. Validated — a name that does not resolve fails at plan/synth, not at run time. Omit and the agent reasons purely over upstream outputs.

Read by: registry.py -> agent.tool -> ctx.call_tool / ctx.retrieve

corpus.description:
For a type="kb" tool: which corpus to retrieve from. Must be one of that tool's declared `corpora`, and the Cedar permit is narrowed to it.

Read by: registry.py -> agent.corpus -> ctx.retrieve(doc_type=)

access.description:
A short human label for the data source, for the UI chip. ONLY read when the agent has no `tool` — with a tool the chip comes from the tool's type, so setting both means this is never shown.

Read by: bff/workflow.py data_source -> the UI chip

longTerm.description:
Long-term memory strategies: "semantic" extracts discrete insights across runs, "summary" keeps a running session summary. The framework recalls before run() and stores after. `true` is shorthand for ["semantic"].

Read by: context.py _longterm_strategies; validated by registry.validate_features

Allowed values (memoryStrategies in app/vocabulary.json): 'semantic', 'summary'

input.description:
Screen this agent's input before the model sees it. Use on any agent that reads text a human typed.

Read by: context.py guardrail("INPUT")

output.description:
Screen this agent's output. Use on any agent handling untrusted text.

Read by: context.py guardrail("OUTPUT")

guardrailId.description:
Use a DIFFERENT guardrail for this one agent, instead of the deployment's own. For a step whose content policy genuinely differs — a medical or legal stage inside a general pipeline. Omit and the deployment guardrail applies.

Read by: context.py guardrail() -> the GuardrailIdentifier on the Bedrock call

enabled.description:
Turn on AgentCore Evaluations for this agent and show its Evaluate button.

Read by: evaluations/service.py is_enabled; bff/workflow.py evalAgents

auto.description:
true scores the agent automatically when the run completes; false means on demand only. Each evaluator is a billed model call, so false is the cheaper default.

Read by: evaluations/service.py is_auto

evaluators.description:
Which judges to run, as Builtin.<Name> or Custom.<Name> — e.g. Builtin.Faithfulness, Builtin.Coherence. Validated on SHAPE, not against a fixed list, so an evaluator AWS adds later needs no framework edit.

Read by: evaluations/service.py evaluators_for; shape-checked by registry.validate_features

Default: ["Builtin.Faithfulness"]

outbound.description:
Credential providers this agent may mint an OAuth token from, to call an external API DIRECTLY. Not needed for anything reached through the Gateway. Required when a remote agent's `auth` is "oauth2".

Read by: context.py get_identity_token

enabled.description:
An app-level Cedar check via ctx.policy_check. Secondary — tool calls through the Gateway are already authorized server-side by the attached engine.

Read by: context.py policy_check

tools.description:
One entry per data source.

One entry per data source, keyed by the tool's label. THE KEY IS BOTH the Gateway target name AND what an agent binds to with its `tool` field, so the two can never drift. Every tool has `type` and `description`; after that the keys depend on the type, because each type is a different kind of Gateway target with different infrastructure. The `call` group is shared by every target that publishes more than one tool. To reach something none of the five types covers — a warehouse, an RDBMS, a VPC service — put it behind a Lambda and use type="lambda": that is the escape hatch, and it needs no framework change.

propertyNames.description: A tool's key must be letters and digits, starting with a letter — it builds both the Gateway target name (no underscores) and the Cedar policy name permit_<key> (no hyphens), so neither separator survives both. Use camelCase, e.g. "policyDocs". An agent id is different and may contain underscores.

type.description:
The kind of Gateway target to create. Closed by what the framework can provision — anything else goes behind a Lambda with type="lambda".

Read by: tools.tf, tool-plane.ts, registry.validate_tool_types, gateway/client.py, the UI chip

Allowed values (toolTypes in app/vocabulary.json): 'kb', 'websearch', 'mcp', 'openapi', 'lambda'

description.description:
Becomes the Gateway target's description. Truncated to 190 characters on deploy.

Read by: tools.tf, tool-plane.ts

corpora.description:
The corpora an agent may retrieve from — one per top-level folder under kb_docs/. An agent scopes itself to one with its `corpus` key.

Read by: tools.tf kb_corpora, kb.tf, tool-plane.ts, TOOLS_JSON

embeddingModel.description:
Which Bedrock model embeds the corpus. Defaults to amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0. Changing it REPLACES the vector index and the Knowledge Base, because neither the model nor the dimension can be altered in place — both IaC paths derive their names from a digest of these properties so that replacement just works instead of failing the deploy.

Read by: kb.tf embed_model, tool-plane.ts embedModel

Allowed values (embeddingModels in app/vocabulary.json): 'amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0', 'amazon.titan-embed-text-v1', 'cohere.embed-english-v3', 'cohere.embed-multilingual-v3'

dimensions.description:
Embedding vector size. Defaults to the first dimension the chosen model lists in vocabulary.json (1024 for Titan v2). Only a value that model supports is accepted: a mismatch is not rejected by Bedrock at deploy time, it fails at INGESTION while the deploy reports success. Lower is cheaper to store and search and slightly less accurate.

Read by: kb.tf kb_dims, tool-plane.ts KB_DIMS

corpusKey.description:
The metadata attribute an agent's `corpus` is matched against. Defaults to "doc_type", which is what this framework's ingestion sidecars write. Set it when your documents are already tagged with something else — a customer id, a product line, a classification — so a corpus need not be a folder name.

Read by: KB_CORPUS_KEY -> kb_lambda/handler.py; the generated Cedar permit

Default: "doc_type"

corpusOperator.description:
How `corpus` is compared against `corpusKey`. Defaults to "equals". Single-value operators only, and that is a boundary rather than an omission: the corpus an agent may read is enforced by a Cedar permit that matches a scalar, so a list-valued operator would weaken it to "has a filter at all".

Read by: KB_CORPUS_OPERATOR -> kb_lambda/handler.py

Allowed values (kbCorpusOperators in app/vocabulary.json): 'equals', 'notEquals', 'startsWith', 'stringContains'

Default: "equals"

filter.description:
A retrieval filter applied to EVERY call, in Bedrock's own filter shape (andAll / orAll / equals / greaterThan / in / ...). This is where multi-condition narrowing goes. It is set on the TARGET and is invisible to the agent, which is the whole point: a filter the agent cannot supply is a boundary, whereas one it passes as an argument is only scoping. ANDed with the agent's own corpus filter, so it narrows and can never widen.

Read by: KB_STATIC_FILTER -> kb_lambda/handler.py

rerank.description:
Rerank retrieved chunks with a second model before they reach the agent. Costs an extra model call per retrieval and usually improves which chunks land in the prompt. Omit for no reranking.

Read by: KB_RERANK -> kb_lambda/handler.py; kb.tf / tool-plane.ts grant the model

model.description: Reranking model id, e.g. "amazon.rerank-v1:0" or "cohere.rerank-v3-5:0". Must be available in the deployment region.

count.description: How many of the retrieved chunks survive reranking. Defaults to `maxResults`. Retrieve more than you keep, or there is nothing for the reranker to reorder.

endpoint.description:
The remote MCP server's Streamable HTTP URL.

Read by: tools.tf, tool-plane.ts

schemaS3Uri.description:
s3:// URI of an OpenAPI schema YOU already host. The framework reads nothing and uploads nothing; it points the Gateway target at this object and grants the Gateway role GetObject on it. Exclusive with source.

Read by: tools.tf, tool-plane.ts

lambdaArn.description:
ARN of a function YOU deployed. The framework registers it and grants the Gateway permission to invoke it; it does not manage its code or its role.

Read by: tools.tf external_lambda_tools, tool-plane.ts

source.description:
Let the framework supply this tool's artifact from orchestrator/app/tools/<source>/ instead of you hosting it, so the committed config names no ARN and no bucket and works in any account. type="lambda" reads handler.py there, zips it and deploys it; type="openapi" reads openapi.json there, uploads it and derives the s3:// URI. Closed to a known set for "lambda" only, because a framework-deployed FUNCTION runs on a role config cannot express; an uploaded SCHEMA needs no permissions, so "openapi" takes any folder name and is checked by whether the file is there. Exclusive with lambdaArn / schemaS3Uri.

Read by: tools.tf builtin_lambda_tools + openapi_source_tools, tool-plane.ts

connectorVersion.description:
Pin the managed web-search connector's version. Omit to take the current one.

Read by: tools.tf, tool-plane.ts

listingMode.description:
How the Gateway discovers the server's tools: DEFAULT caches the catalogue at creation (needed for semantic tool search), DYNAMIC forwards tools/list at invocation time and so never goes stale.

Read by: tools.tf, tool-plane.ts

Allowed values (toolListingModes in app/vocabulary.json): 'DEFAULT', 'DYNAMIC'

Default: "DEFAULT"

call.description:
Which tool on the target to invoke. REQUIRED when the target publishes more than one — the app refuses to guess, because calling the wrong tool returns real-looking data for a question nobody asked.

Read by: TOOLS_JSON -> gateway/client.py _select_tool

arg.description:
The parameter an agent's query goes into. Defaults to "query". This one key is what makes an arbitrary MCP server reachable from config, because every server names its parameters differently.

Read by: TOOLS_JSON -> gateway/client.py _tool_arguments; the Cedar `context.input has <arg>` condition

Default: "query"

args.description:
Fixed extra arguments sent on every call, e.g. a page size.

Read by: TOOLS_JSON -> gateway/client.py

rowPath.description:

steps.description: The topology, in order. Each step runs one agent, a `parallel` group (concurrently, joined at one gate) or a `sequence` group (one after another, one gate after both). Add `hitl` for a human review gate, `branch` to let the step's OWN OUTPUT choose what runs next. A step has no `type` discriminator, so every key here applies to every step — but three of them are mutually exclusive and two only mean anything on a group.

agent.description:
Run this one agent. The id must exist in the `agents` block.

Read by: config.step_agents, graph_builder

parallel.description:
Run these agents CONCURRENTLY and join. `branch` is rejected on a parallel step, because there is no single decider.

Read by: config.step_agents, graph_builder

sequence.description:
Run these agents one after another, with one gate after all of them — so a revise re-runs the whole chain.

Read by: config.step_agents, graph_builder

hitl.description:
Pause after this step for a human to approve, revise or deny. Revise re-runs the step with the reviewer's comment as feedback.

Read by: graph_builder gate nodes and routers

gateId.description:
A name for a GROUP step's gate, which is also the name a `branch` uses to route to this step. Defaults to group<i>. Inert on a single-agent step, whose gate is always <agent>_gate.

Read by: graph_builder _gate_id / _step_name; index.html

gateName.description:
The gate's display name, shown to the reviewer. Falls back to gateId.

Read by: graph_builder group/sequence gate nodes; index.html

branch.description:
Let this step's output pick the next step: {"when": [rules], "default": "<step>"}. Each rule needs `goto` plus at least one comparison, and may name a `field` (a dot path into the output JSON) or omit it to match the raw text. Rejected on a parallel step and on the last step.

Read by: graph_builder validate_branches / make_branch_node; branching.py

allOf.$comment: A step runs one agent, a concurrent group or a chained group. Anything else has no meaning, and both the graph builder and the topology derivation assume exactly one.

defaultModel.description:
Model for any agent that does not name its own. BEDROCK_MODEL_ID overrides it.

Read by: config.py MODEL_ID

Default: "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"

modelRates.description:
Per-model token rates keyed by a substring of the model id, e.g. {"nova-pro": {"input": 0.80, "output": 3.20}} in USD per million. Set this for your own model — an unknown one is priced at a fallback and the telemetry row is marked rates_known=false.

Read by: config.py MODEL_RATES -> observability/pricing.py

chatbot.description:
The in-app assistant: enabled, model, greeting, placeholder, and a `tools` map of per-capability flags (anything unlisted defaults to ON).

Read by: bff/chatbot.py and the bff/workflow.py projection to the browser

orchestrator.description: Engine-wide settings. Not an agent — it has no model or prompt of its own. Not reordered by the formatter: there is only ONE of these blocks, so there is no second one to read consistently against.

guardrail.description: The Bedrock Guardrail POLICY — what is enforced. Which agents it is applied to is per agent, in agentcore.guardrails. Omit any key and that policy block is not created at all; omit the whole block for an empty guardrail. Read only by the IaC: the app just gets a GUARDRAIL_ID.

groupsClaim.description:
The JWT claim holding the caller's groups. Defaults to "cognito:groups".

Read by: bff/authz.py

Default: "cognito:groups"

actions.description:
Action -> the group names allowed to take it. Each action name is a route in bff/handler.py; one with no route would read as a restriction and gate nothing. An action you omit is UNRESTRICTED.

Read by: bff/authz.py; bff/workflow.py projects it to the UI

Allowed keys (authorizationActions in app/vocabulary.json): 'start', 'decision', 'rerun', 'cancel', 'evaluate', 'insights', 'delete'

authorization.description: Who may act on a run. An action ABSENT from the `actions` map is unrestricted, so this block is an opt-in list of restrictions rather than a full policy. Enforced in the BFF, and projected to the UI so it can disable a control it knows will 403 instead of offering it and failing.
